faq.q: How many cameras will my property need?
faq.a: It depends on the layout, not a fixed number. During a site survey we identify entry points, vulnerable areas and coverage overlaps, then propose the minimum set of cameras that covers your property properly.

faq.q: Can I view my cameras on my mobile phone?
faq.a: Yes. We configure secure remote viewing on your smartphone so you can see live and recorded footage from anywhere with an internet connection.

faq.q: How long can footage be stored?
faq.a: Storage is sized to your requirement — commonly a few weeks of continuous recording. We recommend the appropriate hard disk capacity based on camera count, resolution and retention needs.

faq.q: Do the cameras work at night?
faq.a: Yes, we use cameras with infrared or low-light capability for night coverage, so entrances, compounds and stores remain monitored after dark.

faq.q: Do you provide service for existing CCTV systems?
faq.a: Yes, we take up maintenance and troubleshooting of CCTV systems, including camera replacement, DVR/NVR issues and cabling faults. Contact us with details of your current system.

faq.q: Analog HD or IP cameras — which should I choose?
faq.a: Both have their place. Analog HD is cost-effective over existing coaxial cabling; IP cameras offer higher resolution and flexibility over network cabling. We recommend based on your site, budget and quality needs rather than one-size-fits-all.

faq.q: What is the difference between audio and video intercoms?
faq.a: An audio intercom lets you speak with the visitor; a video intercom (video door phone) also shows you a live camera view of them at the door. Video models add an important layer of verification, especially at night.

faq.q: Can one entrance panel call multiple flats or offices?
faq.a: Yes. Multi-unit intercom systems allow visitors to dial a flat or office number from a common entrance panel, with each unit having its own indoor station.

faq.q: Can the intercom unlock the gate or door?
faq.a: Many intercom systems support electric lock or gate release from the indoor station, so you can let in a verified visitor without walking to the door. We will advise on compatibility during survey.

faq.q: Will installation damage my walls?
faq.a: We plan wiring routes carefully. Where possible, cabling is concealed; otherwise neat casing is used. We treat finished homes and offices with care and clean up after the work.

faq.q: Do you service old intercom systems?
faq.a: We take up intercom repair and troubleshooting where parts are available, and can advise honestly when replacement is more sensible than repair.

faq.q: Do you take up office networking projects?
faq.a: Yes. Office LAN setup and structured cabling are core services for us — from small offices to multi-floor commercial buildings, including racks, patch panels, switches and Wi-Fi.

faq.q: CAT6 or CAT6A — what do I need?
faq.a: For most offices, CAT6 is sufficient and cost-effective. CAT6A suits higher bandwidth and longer runs, such as busy backbones or future-proofing for 10G. We recommend based on measured distances and actual usage.

faq.q: Can you fix networks installed by someone else?
faq.a: Yes. We frequently take over undocumented or poorly installed networks — re-terminating, re-organising racks, testing links and bringing the setup to a maintainable standard.

faq.q: Can you provide Wi-Fi coverage for an entire building?
faq.a: Yes. We plan access point positions based on the building layout and construction, so coverage is even and speeds are consistent rather than depending on a single overloaded router.

faq.q: Do you handle fiber optic cabling?
faq.a: Where a project needs fiber links — for distance, bandwidth or interference reasons — we include fiber cabling in the design. Tell us your requirement and we will advise.

faq.q: Do you provide biometric attendance systems?
faq.a: Yes. We supply and install fingerprint and face-recognition attendance systems for offices, factories, schools and other organisations, including reporting software and staff training.

faq.q: Fingerprint or face recognition — which is better?
faq.a: Fingerprint devices are proven and economical. Face-recognition terminals are touchless and faster at gates, and work well where fingers are worn by manual work. We recommend based on your workforce and usage points.

faq.q: Can the same device control a door lock?
faq.a: Yes. Most access-control devices can drive an electric lock, so the same credential that marks attendance can also allow or deny entry through a door.

faq.q: What happens if the device or network fails?
faq.a: Attendance devices store records locally and sync when connectivity returns, so punches are not lost during brief failures. We configure and advise appropriately for your site.

faq.q: Can we get monthly attendance reports for payroll?
faq.a: Yes. The software generates daily, monthly and shift-wise reports — late-coming, overtime, absentees — which can be exported for payroll processing.

faq.q: Do you supply fire extinguishers?
faq.a: Yes. We supply fire extinguishers including ABC dry chemical powder, CO2, foam and other types, along with fire buckets and safety accessories, for businesses and institutions.

faq.q: Which extinguisher type does my premises need?
faq.a: It depends on the fire risks present. Offices generally need ABC dry powder; electrical and server areas need CO2; fuel or solvent storage areas need foam or dry powder. We assess your site and recommend accordingly.

faq.q: Do you provide refilling services?
faq.a: Yes, we support refilling of extinguishers after use or on expiry of their service interval, along with the required records. Contact us with your extinguisher details.

faq.q: How often should extinguishers be inspected?
faq.a: Extinguishers should be visually checked regularly (pressure gauge, seals, access) and serviced on the interval marked by the manufacturer. We can include periodic inspection visits for your premises.

faq.q: Can you tell us where extinguishers should be installed?
faq.a: Yes. Placement matters — along escape routes, near exits, at risk areas, mounted at correct height with signage. We plan placement as part of supply.
